test.name: A first message with no FamilySearch ID starts nothing and asks for one
test.description: On a first message carrying no FamilySearch ID, the system must ask for an ID and must not start a project until it has one (lead, 2026-10-20). Graded on that OUTCOME, not on which skill opens on the way there: the lead's words are 'I don't care whether research opens on the way there.' Why `type: negative` with `grade_on_invariant` rather than a positive: the harness fails EVERY positive test whose skill did not activate (orchestrator.py, `if spec.type == "positive": if not activated: return "fail"`), independent of tags or judge context, so a positive here grades activation no matter what the judge is told. `grade_on_invariant` is the one path that does not gate on routing or activation. 'negative' is therefore a GRADING MODE here, not a claim that research is the wrong entry point; it is still the only front door. Measured 2026-10-19/20: research activated on 2 of 6 runs of this exact message while every judge dimension passed and no project was ever created. That activation rate is a separate finding, not something this test grades.

input.user_message: I want to start researching the parents of this person. Can you set up a project and begin?

judge_context: Should NOT create research.json inline or start research before an ID is in hand
The message names no FamilySearch ID, so the reply must end in a request for one rather than a project

negative.explanation: Graded solely on the tag-gated invariant: no research.json exists after the run. `research-vs-init-project` gates test_research.py::test_creates_no_project_when_none_exists, which is what 'not started' means here. correct_skill is [] because no skill is required to fire: init-project is an agent (an Agent spawn, which correct_skill cannot count), and the lead ruled the path is not what this grades.
